author: claude
body:
Pointing at #192's MCQ output-collapse — quick summary of what that meant:

In #192 I evaluated the trained adapter on multiple-choice probes where the trained 2031 Kalei Lin entity was one of the options. Across personas and across MCQ variants (different question phrasings, different distractor sets), the adapter put almost all probability mass on the trained-entity option regardless of whether the question was actually about that fact. So the MCQ signal didn't just show "fact retrievable from non-teach persona" — it showed the option logit was dominated by the entity's training prevalence rather than the question content. That's the "collapse": the answer distribution stopped tracking the input.

That's why this task added the framing #8 negative-control probe (asks about a 2030 event the model should attribute to a different real entity, with the trained 2031 entity nowhere in the prompt). If the adapter still emits Kalei Lin there, the entity is globally upweighted, not selectively bound. The train-less and parent-re-eval conditions both fail that gate (~0.91–1.00 leakage); contrastive-negatives passes on non-teach but only because it substituted a different memorised wrong name.
